items.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: He said “why don’t you just do it like a Tommy Dorsey arrangement” or Les Brown or whatever, swing bands.

ctx.x: I see. So you were like scraping for material.

Yeah. It didn’t make any sense. And that’s when I switched over to doing “Night Sound,” “Blue Angel,” “I Get a Kick out of Porter,” because I had Cole Porter’s music to work with. And the Irving Berlin album. That was based on his 50th year as a composer. And I used “I Love A Piano” as a theme song, which he wrote in 1917, the year after I was born, and I got to know Irving. I did the Bell Telephone Hour when they did an Irving © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -17-

Berlin special and he was there and I was delighted to hang out with him. And I went over and saw him, I only lived a couple of blocks from Beekman Place where Berlin lived. We were on Sutton. And I went over and had some coffee with him and to discuss it. And I thought of doing a 50th, because you can get almost 30 minutes on an LP side. And even the ballad would not take more than a minute, that’s why usually back in those days the single records always were two and a half minutes or three minutes. And so I…
